readme:
# Inert anticyclotomic CM main conjecture

This roadmap plans the global arithmetic consequences of the integral signed decomposition at an inert prime. Its first endpoint is BKO21 Theorem 6.1 (p.962): the dual with sign opposite the functional equation is torsion, with integral characteristic ideal generated by Rubin’s anticyclotomic p-adic L-function. Its second endpoint is Theorem 6.2 (pp.962–963), a finite-character CM rank bound, with a possible extra local dimension in one parity.

The parent is **ModularIwasawaMainConjectures**. This is a separate inert-CM branch: no ordinary theorem, split-prime hypothesis, epsilon conjecture or Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer equality is imported as an endpoint. The standing hypothesis is p≥5 inert and p∤h_K. The main-conjecture theorem permits the Gross Q-curve only over H. The finite-rank theorem adds E/K. Neither general statement assumes 2 splits.

This is a completed planning pass, with every layer planned and implementation unchecked. Four explicit source/proof gaps and the supplier requests below prevent mathematical closure. In particular the inert translation of Rubin's two-variable theorem, the two-variable relaxed/strict comparison and the full Gross normalization argument remain open; the endpoint statements are targets, not claims of completed proofs.

## Conventions and the arithmetic objects

The standing hypotheses for every target are:

1. p≥5 is prime and inert in the imaginary quadratic field K; p does not divide h_K. H is the Hilbert class field.
2. φ has infinity type (1,0), conductor f prime to p, φ((α))=α for α≡1 mod f, and φ(conjugate(a))=conjugate(φ(a)). The character φ∘N_(H/K) belongs to a maximal-CM Gross Q-curve E/H with good reduction above p.
3. Φ=K_p is unramified quadratic over Q_p, O its integers, π=−p, and F/O is the imported Lubin–Tate formal O-module. The fixed complex and p-adic embeddings, smooth model and differential give a period lattice Ω O_K.
4. R is the integer ring of a finite extension L/Φ containing the p-adic avatar φ_p. T=R(φ_p), W=T⊗_O(Φ/O)≃(T⊗_R L)/T. Λ_R=R[[Γ⁻]], Γ⁻=Gal(K∞/K)≃Z_p; ε=W(φ)∈{+1,−1}.

For every finite-rank/control target the extra hypothesis is: For finite-level rank/control statements E descends to K, and the chosen CM component of V_pE is T⊗_R L. Character values lie in a finite extension Lχ/L; dimensions are over Lχ.

Write H for the Hilbert class field only in the arithmetic setup; in the local-cohomology comparison write H_Iw for the compact local limit (the target formulas abbreviate that module as H). T′ always denotes the Cartier-dual lattice, with the inverse-different coefficient trace pairing. It is not silently T. The local O-module and its signed lattices are the ones supplied by AnticyclotomicLocalUnits. Λ_R is the coefficient ring throughout. Restriction to O uses the norm of a characteristic ideal; it does not leave its generator unchanged.

Here are three sign conventions which must be checked together:

| object | convention | low-level check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| finite χ of exact order p^r, r≥1 | conductor exponent c=r+1; least layer K_r | orders p,p² give exponents 2,3 |
| BKO character sets | Ξ⁺ has even conductor exponent; Ξ⁻ has odd exponent | 1∈Ξ⁺, order p∈Ξ⁺, order p²∈Ξ⁻ |
| AH character sets | Ξ_AH^s=Ξ_BKO^(−s) | 1∈Ξ_AH⁻ |
| formal points of sign s | kill the BKO characters in Ξ^s | the trivial rational point component lies in A⁻ |
| compact signed units of sign s | derivatives vanish at Ξ^(−s) | a basis of V^s is detected at Ξ^s |
| signed Selmer sign | AH and BKO same-label local conditions agree | the ordinary χ-part for χ∈Ξ^ε is in Sel_(−ε) |
| dual Γ-action | (γf)(x)=f(γ⁻¹x) | evaluation pairs χ with χ⁻¹ |

The trivial character has exponent c=0 and least layer K_0. For any χ, use n≥max(c−1,0); BKO’s source indexing K_c is also a permissible deeper layer. One must not require a degree-p^c extension to be the least field of definition. For interpolation, δ_1=(1+p⁻¹)δ is used as supplied by ALU. At ε=− the trivial derivative of the signed line is zero, so a nontrivial-character quotient formula cannot be extended to χ=1 by substitution.

## Ownership, current libraries and direct imports

The accepted BKO extraction’s corrected routes 5–6 place the **late** primitive ξ, C∞ and Rubin L_p construction here. NonordinaryCMSpecialValues retains the early Gross/CM classes, root numbers and special-value nonvanishing; ALU retains their exact local projection and explicit reciprocity comparison. This ordering breaks the apparent cycle in the older brief that imported the finished L-function from the early owner.

AnticyclotomicLocalUnits supplies its actual carriers and exact nodes: ALU.0/conductor-parity; ALU.2/anticyclotomic-kummer-pairing; ALU.3/signed-formal-points, signed-annihilator and character-logarithm; ALU.4/projected-cm-class, cm-class-values and wiles-dual-exponential; ALU.8/integral-signed-decomposition, signed-generator-nonvanishing and finite-signed-point-export. Their blueprint status remains unchecked, and their own upstream gaps are inherited. We neither reprove the local conjecture nor introduce another trace-defined signed point space.

The general Kummer and discrete Selmer carrier belongs to current TauCetiRoadmap **EllipticCurves Layer 7**. SelmerIwasawaCohomology supplies the compact/discrete extensions, orthogonals, inverse limits, descent and kernel-control interfaces; ArithmeticGaloisDuality supplies R02.4 lattice/rational Poitou–Tate. PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L4/L5 owns characteristic ideals, their exact-sequence and coefficient APIs, finite errors and generic specialization algebra; it is now the TauCetiRoadmap roadmap of that name, whose §4.6 states these targets. CMAllPrimeMainConjectures CZ.2 owns the elliptic-unit Euler system and Rubin's two-variable main conjecture (Rubin 1991, Theorem 4.1). For p inert its part (ii) is a class-group/global-units equality on the χ-parts nontrivial on the decomposition group of p; IC.3 translates it to the strict and relaxed Selmer modules of the Gross avatar. This roadmap only instantiates these suppliers for the inert CM datum.

The reviewed library audit was read for the duality, Selmer/Iwasawa and characteristic-algebra stages (AUDIT-02, AUDIT-27 and AUDIT-26). Their full signed arithmetic carriers and comparison theorems are not in the pinned libraries. The existing explicit 2-descent SelmerGroup is a nearby result, not the general p≥5 cohomological Selmer carrier. Current Tau Ceti already has the native completed group algebra and the compact-module action in its CompletedGroupAlgebra Basic/Module files; these are reused through the supplier interface, never planned afresh. Those current additions are not silently treated as declarations at the older pins.

The current upstream ProfiniteArithmetic, ArithmeticDirichletSeries and RepresentationTheory reader documents were checked, together with EllipticCurves’ Selmer and formal-group layers and the current Tau Ceti library. The profinite completion/topological module and ordinary Dirichlet-series infrastructure stays with those owners. It does not supply the specialized Gross elliptic-unit comparison. At the pins, Module.Basis (including its repr field) and Ideal.span_singleton_mul_left_unit were read directly; these support only the small coordinate facet of the suggested file.

## How the proof is assembled

The first two layers identify arithmetic towers, coefficients, points and Selmer kernels before any global rank is asserted. The primitive class is then put in its signed line and its integral coordinate is defined. The global all-auxiliary module remains a distinct object: interpolation of one local vector does not prove equality with its localized global lattice.

The integral two-variable theorem gives char(X_str)=char(S_rel/C), after the specialization correction divisor is proved common to both sides. Global duality gives the signed exact sequence. Its rank argument proves opposite signed torsion and vanishing of the compact strict kernel; its two quotient sequences then give char(X_(−ε))=char(H_Iw^ε/loc(C)). The final normalization target identifies this last ideal with the primitive (L_p), integrally over Λ_R. Each of these equalities is a separate target, so the missing integral input cannot hide inside a restatement of the final theorem.

For finite ranks, the signed control polynomials split the finite character sets only after finite integral errors are accounted for. Matching characters are bounded using the torsion opposite signed dual. Other characters use the strict characteristic divisor and the one-dimensional CM local correction. A Kummer injection supplies the lower bound by the Mordell–Weil CM rank. None of this asserts rank equality, a leading-term formula or an epsilon-factor statement.

## Layers and their targets

All target formulas below use the standing hypotheses above; additional assumptions are displayed at the target. Source matches explain which argument is supported and where a new comparison is still needed. A Check is an acceptance criterion for the eventual formalization, not a claim of an existing Lean proof.

stages.title: The inert CM datum and the tower dictionary
stages.description:
Specify the Gross datum and coefficients, identify global and local towers and conductor indices, transport the local avatar and dual lattice, and extend the proved local signed decomposition to R.

Targets: The inert Gross CM datum; Global and local anticyclotomic towers; Order, conductor and sign dictionary; The local discrete CM module; Signed decomposition over the CM coefficient ring.

stages.title: Signed Kummer images and global Selmer kernels
stages.description:
Transport the actual same-parity formal-point Kummer images, prove independence and away-p rational vanishing, then instantiate the imported discrete and compact Selmer carriers with their contragredient actions.

Targets: Transported signed Kummer conditions; Independence of the local CM comparison; Rational local vanishing away from p; The four global CM Selmer conditions; Infinite Selmer duals and compact Selmer modules.

stages.title: The primitive class and Rubin’s integral L-function
stages.description:
Use the primitive ν=1 CM class, prove its root-number sign and nonvanishing, define its integral signed coordinate and lattice, and establish interpolation with the inverse-character derivative and a separate trivial case.

Targets: The primitive global CM elliptic-unit class; Primitive and imprimitive special values; Sign and nonvanishing of the primitive class; Rubin’s integral anticyclotomic p-adic L-function; Interpolation with inverse-character denominator.

stages.title: Global elliptic units and strict comparison
stages.description:
Construct the full auxiliary-ideal global module, establish the Gross descent and local dictionary, prove the relaxed/strict ranks, and specialize the integral inert two-variable elliptic-unit theorem (Rubin 1991 Theorem 4.1(ii), imported from CMAllPrimeMainConjectures CZ.2) with its correction divisor retained.

Targets: The all-auxiliary global elliptic-unit module; Gross Q-curve and coefficient descent contracts; Compact local cohomology and signed local units; The relaxed and strict global ranks; Integral elliptic-unit comparison for the strict dual.

stages.title: Global duality and the integral main conjecture
stages.description:
Prove the exact signed duality sequences, opposite torsion, relaxed-dual characteristic comparison, and the primitive local-lattice normalization; conclude the integral characteristic identity over Λ_R.

Targets: The signed global-duality sequence; Opposite signed torsion and vanishing compact kernels; Torsion in the relaxed dual; From global units to the opposite signed characteristic ideal; The localized global lattice and the primitive class; The inert anticyclotomic CM main conjecture.

stages.title: Finite-level signed and strict control
stages.description:
Use the exact signed cyclotomic polynomials, prove local and global signed control with finite errors, compare the two finite signed components, and prove the strict specialization inequality from injectivity of restriction and the bound of a specialization's dimension by the local length.

Targets: The signed finite-level annihilators; Signed local control with its finite error; Signed Selmer control at finite level; Finite-level decomposition into the two signed pieces; Specialization dimension is bounded by the local length; Strict Selmer specialization inequality.

stages.title: Finite-character CM rank bounds
stages.description:
Prove strict divisor containment, the local CM codimension-one bound, and the matching signed Selmer bound; combine them with Kummer injectivity to obtain both parity cases of the finite-character rank inequality.

Targets: The strict characteristic divisor divides L_p; The one-dimensional CM local correction; The matching-parity Selmer bound; Finite-character CM rank bounds.
